page: Microsoft Azure M24s_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the MSMediumMemoryv3 family. Powered by an x86_64 Intel processor running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the platform supplies 24 dedicated virtual CPUs alongside 480.0 GB of system memory. This hardware allocation yields a high memory density of 20.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, specifically tailored to support environments requiring extensive working memory spaces without requiring excessive core allocations.

Hardware acceleration is omitted, with zero discrete GPUs present. The instance does not include integrated local disk capacity, reporting a local storage size of None. Storage requirements are met through network-attached volumes, with native support for Azure Premium Storage for high-throughput persistence. System administrators must factor in external disk connectivity and separate public IPv4 provisioning, as zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled with the instance by default.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, the 20:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio offers favorable resource consolidation for memory-bound applications, mitigating the need to license and scale unneeded compute capacity solely to acquire additional RAM. Tradeoffs include total reliance on remote storage systems for both root file systems and application data. The instance is technically targeted at memory-intensive enterprise tasks, such as in-memory databases, data caching fabrics, large relational database engines, and heavy analytics operations.
